Lemma
[existence of a subordinate partition of unity]

↗ thm:dc-ch0-5-6

1. ch0:5.6Let $M$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable (equivalently $\sigma $-compact), finite-dimensional differentiable manifold. For every closed set $s\subseteq M$ and every open covering $\{ U_i\} $ of $s$ there is a differentiable partition of unity $\{ f_i\} $ subordinate to $\{ U_i\} $, i.e. with $\operatorname {supp} f_i\subseteq U_i$.
Proof

\sketch

Hausdorffness and second countability make $M$ paracompact and $\sigma $-compact. Local Euclidean bump functions supported in the $U_i$ form a locally finite family; normalizing their sum yields the required partition.

□
